summary.intent: Complete Phase 48 post-implementation validation: run CodeRabbit CLI review and a security review in parallel, then apply all actionable findings before committing the phase.
summary.outcome: Security review assessed overall risk as LOW (zero-knowledge invariant holds, crypto correct); CodeRabbit surfaced 5 findings of which 4 were applied (per-row ciphertext guard, 3x DTO MaxLength widening, SDK key-zeroing on unmount) and 1 resolved by deletion (.env.dev-backup). All CI gates pass.

repo: pnpm typecheck does not include apps/api — api typechecking runs via nest build (tsconfig.build.json excludes **/*spec.ts) in a separate CI job, so spec-file type errors never hit the shared typecheck gate
@MaxLength decorators on NestJS DTOs are NOT emitted to the OpenAPI spec, so bumping them requires no api:generate and won't dirty openapi.json
unloadSharedFolder(shareId) is never called from any web production code path — the SDK's cloned shared-folder keys are only zeroed at GC time unless explicitly unloaded
The share store (fetchReceivedShares result) is in-memory only; there is a comment confirming 'never persisted in this form', making plaintext-retention a non-issue
.env.dev-backup was untracked and not covered by .gitignore — a live secrets file silently present in the working tree
A pre-existing HttpArgumentsHost type error in http-metrics.interceptor.spec.ts exists on origin/main and CI is green, confirming specs are excluded from the api typecheck gate

code.finding: fetchReceivedShares decrypted itemName inside Promise.all with no per-row guard — a single corrupt or mismatched ciphertext row would reject the entire received-shares list. Fixed with per-row try/catch falling back to s.itemName.
Projection-subscription effect cleanup only called unsubscribe(); it never called unloadSharedFolder(shareId), so the SDK's cloned shared-folder key material was never explicitly zeroed on unmount.
@MaxLength(1024) on itemNameEncrypted was too small — ECIES ciphertext for a 255-char multibyte (CJK/emoji) name can reach ~1724 hex chars, causing a 400 on create. Bumped to 2500.
Same @MaxLength(1024) too-small bug on itemNameEncrypted as create-share.dto.ts. Bumped to 2500.
Same @MaxLength(1024) too-small bug on itemNameEncrypted. Bumped to 2500.

workflow: CodeRabbit CLI can be run with --agent --base-commit <sha> to produce structured findings scoped to a phase diff; cloud reviews take 5–15 min for large diffs so parallelizing with a security review recovers that wait time
Capturing exit codes through pipes (e.g. tsc | tail) masks the real exit code — always capture separately or check $PIPESTATUS to avoid false 'exit 0' reads
Committing with explicit git add <file> (never -A or .) is a safe-by-default guard against accidentally staging .env* files or large binaries

friction: .env.dev-backup was not gitignored and contained real secrets — required surfacing to the user and explicit authorization before deletion; Bash restrictions on .env* files blocked autonomous action
CodeRabbit's exit code and output piped through tail masked the tsc exit code, causing a false 'all green' read that required a second run to verify
CodeRabbit cloud review takes 5–15 min, creating a blocking wait window before findings can be batched
